9/10 A solid entry in a fantastic series with great new characters and the return of a series icon. Grace's sections are tense while as Leon you are a seasoned agent, going John Wick on enemies without breaking a sweat. A little campy sometimes but it's done with charm and if you love this series you can't help smiling. Replayability is fun on different difficulties because the gameplay is crisp and the enemies act differently on higher difficulties, rather than becoming bullet sponges. Very much looking forward to what they do with the Veronica remake following this!

The Good

At first I was a bit scared that they decided to bring Leon back, that it would be a weaker RE game, but I can say that after I 100% it. It was a really good mix of survival horror and action horror. The horror parts with Grace were scary where they were supposed to be and Capcom did an incredible job. For me it is the 2nd or 3rd most scary game from RE franchise.
The action horror parts with Leon on the gameplay part, are better then RE4 remake, the combat is just amazing.
The story isn't best from all RE games, but it is still really good.

The Bad

There are some very slow parts that are really annoying when you are replaying it and it wasn't the most fun RE game to replay.
I didn't really like that there are infinite saves for speed demon challenge (challenge that you need to complete the game in 4 hours) because when I was speedrunning other RE games the limited saves added an interesting prespective to it, because you needed to be really careful when to save the game.
Easily one of the best Resident Evil games of all time and the first one that I have played to full completion.

Resident Evil is on an absolutely generational run. Requiem combines the best aspects of the previous games and puts it into a perfect package of nostalgia and creative new content. If you liked RE4 and RE7, this game slaps both of them together into a seamless blend of action and horror.

Having played all of the mainline games and their remakes, I’d say this is probably one of the best modern Resident Evil games.

It’s also the most scared I’ve felt playing an RE game since the Shadows of Rose DLC, although that’s probably more true on the first playthrough. The game pulls in a lot of ideas from previous entries: the creepy mansion, a stalker enemy, and Leon’s section being much more action-focused—basically RE4, except Leon is even more badass. There are also some fantastic action set pieces, including a motorcycle chase like RE6 and a close combat fight like RE4 Krauser.

Overall, this game was an absolute blast to play. My first playthrough took damn near 18 hours, although a lot of that came from me constantly resetting because I had wasted resources or taken too much damage. On subsequent playthroughs, the game becomes much more enjoyable because you know the layouts, encounters, and what you actually need to worry about.

The only thing that gets worse with repeated playthroughs is the Chloe section. On a first playthrough, it’s genuinely scary, but on subsequent runs I really wish it could be skipped entirely or replaced with a cutscene. I feel similarly about the Wrenwood opening.

Other than those two tedious sections, though, this is genuinely one of the best games the series has to offer.

It's Resident Evil, so you know what you're getting except in Requiem it's dialled up to 11.

Requiem has you playing 2 protagonists: Grace Ashcroft and Leon Kennedy (back with his knee slapping 1 liners) 
Only this time it isn't done like in RE2 where you play each character as separate arcs but instead the game will frequently interchange between both of them depending on the story.
This leads to the selling point of RE9 (at least for me) which is each protagonist bringing with their own playstyle. To put it simply: Grace's gameplay plays like Ethan Winters from RE7 + 8 and Leon's is, well Leon from RE4. The end result is a nice balance of 'tension and release' pacing, going between feeling like a prey then to the predator.

I believe there's a free demo you can try. The demo is only a small portion from the opening of the game but it lets you play as Grace then Leon. The rest of the game will pretty much play in that fashion.

I don't usually write reviews, but this game deserves one.

I've been playing games for years, and I can honestly say Resident Evil Requiem is the best game I've played in all my years of gaming.

Everything just clicked. The atmosphere, the gameplay, the story, the music, the visuals—every part of it felt like it was made with care. I was hooked from the beginning and couldn't wait to see what happened next.

Leon was amazing to play as, and Grace was a fantastic new character. I really liked how different they felt, and both of their stories kept me invested the whole way through.

I genuinely don't have a single complaint. Every chapter had something memorable, and the game never felt boring or dragged on. By the time the credits rolled, I was already thinking about starting another playthrough.

For me, this is a 10/10 masterpiece and easily my favorite Resident Evil game. More than that, it's the best game I've played in all my years of gaming.

Capcom absolutely knocked it out of the park.

I don't normally buy games at $70, especially ones that are roughly 17 hours long, but I felt like treating myself this time.

Resident Evil Requiem is basically a perfect blend of RE4/RE5 action with Resident Evil 7. The game swaps between two characters, one experiencing the horror elements seen in RE7 (Grace), and then to break those parts up, it swaps to action (Leon).

Both segments are built really well. There are a few over the top 'Chris punching a boulder' levels of ridiculousness towards the end (Especially at one segment), and I felt like Leon's long stretch of game play overstayed it's welcome, but that's more of a personal preference than a real criticism. I like Resident Evil for being scary.

Definitely worth it on sale, I think it's maybe $20 expensive for my standards, but great game either way.

A pretty good Resident Evil game. While there are a few minor things I could criticize, the worst offenders are the handguns and upgrades why do some of the weapons actually end up looking worse after you upgrade them again ? Don’t even get me started on the suppressed handgunit felt like some kind of CoD black ops 2 nonsense. They definitely could have included another normal handgun like a modern 1911 but I suppose that’s what mods are for. I also avoided wearing the body armor because it just looked terrible yet, toward the end, the character ends up wearing it anyway in the cutscenes even though I never bought it. When you upgrade the Requiem, the grip is supposed to turn white but ingame nothing changes. The axe, on the other hand, does change its appearance, which only makes it look worse. Well, they certainly made some questionable design choices in that regard. Also one of the weaker games in terms of replayability overall still pretty SOLID must play for RE fans.

One of the best modern Resident Evil games, deadass. I don't think there's been another mainline entry in the last 5 years that could top this. Not only does it tie up loose knots in the overall timeline, it gives us a bunch of more depth for Leon. Anybody who says this game is bad is just wrong. You should pick this up, whether you're a long-time enjoyer of the franchise, or trying to get into it.

I did receive this for free only because it came with my new MAG monitor, but I was 100% going to buy it anyway.

Requiem is one of the best games this year and by far one of the best ever RE games. I don't know how a RE fan couldn't enjoy this - you have the best of both worlds: really great survival horror and puzzle solving, mixed with really fun action scenes and gunplay with Leon, along with his trademark laugh out loud lines. I wouldn't say that it does any of these the best (RE7 for horror & ofc RE4 for action), but the fact that it does them all and pulls them off so well is worth the applause.

Intriguing enough story, maybe some minor plot holes here and there but I still enjoyed the narrative and acting. Can't wait for Veronica and future RE projects. Capcom really is on a remarkable run at the moment. I hope that they can continue to keep it up and not slip up again.
